correctness.rationale: Every proper ideal of k[x,y]/(xy,x^m,y^n), 3<=m<n, is uniquely a monomial pair of branch tails or a one-dimensional diagonal boundary slope. All automorphisms preserve the branch labels and consist of invertible branch jets with independent nonzero leading scalars and two socle shears. The latter create precisely two q-element orbits combining a monomial endpoint with q-1 mixed slopes. Each other mixed exponent pair is preserved and has a cyclic scalar-ratio action with image cardinality (q-1)/gcd(u,v,q-1). This gives exhaustive orbit-size counts and the characteristic-ideal count; dimensions follow from explicit basis tails. Exact finite subspace/ideal/orbit enumeration independently agrees with all formulas for (m,n,q)=(3,4,2),(3,4,3),(3,4,5),(3,5,2),(3,5,3),(4,5,2). The proof, not these finite computations, covers all finite fields and lengths. Boundaries and normalizations are explicit in RESULT.md.

value.rationale: An exact classification of orbits of the full automorphism group on all ideals is a natural equivariant invariant of a classical family of Artinian local rings. It determines the complete orbit-size distribution with gcd arithmetic, an exact dimension-refined characteristic-ideal count, and the striking all-length binary rigidity of precisely four nonfixed ideals. This is not a single tiny numerical gain, an arbitrary parameter slice, or merely a recurrence: it solves a natural all-parameter orbit problem and shows a sharp finite-field arithmetic shift. The case m<n is mathematically needed to prevent branch-swapping, and the nilpotency-length >=3 boundary is needed for cotangent rigidity.
